A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the palatine tonsil of the adult human is an organ of the immune system, which is characterized by the presence of all classes of immunoglobulin, with a predominance of IgM, IgG and IgA.
the tonsillar lymphoid tissue of normal subjects is dominated by IgG immunocytes, with IgA cells constituting the next largest group, and IgM and IgD cells the smallest.
the immunocyte population of the human tonsil, in the absence of disease, is characterized by a high proportion of IgG-producing cells, and that this is a feature of tonsils of all ages.
